title: Birthday Cards
summary: Scalloped florals, a big script hello, and a birthday card that looks nothing like the drugstore rack.
story: Birthday cards are drawn around one person. Some are a floral border and a loose script greeting. Others turn the year into a little illustration — an object, a joke, a color they actually wear. The lettering is the point: their name, the age if you want it said out loud, and a line you would say if you handed it over yourself.
includes: Hand-lettered greeting on the front
An original illustration, floral or playful
Room for a note inside
A clear sleeve when you want it gift-ready
madeFor: Birthdays that deserve more than a printed verse
Milestone years
The friend who keeps every card
note: Send the name, the date, and any line that has to be in there. A favorite color helps.

title: Thank-You Cards
summary: Striped paper, brush script, and a ribbon-tied set for the notes you keep meaning to send.
story: Thank-you cards are a studio staple: sage and cream stripes, a single script phrase, and a stack you can actually finish. Order one for a host, or a small set tied in a ribbon for the people who showed up — a shower, a dinner, a market neighbor, a whole guest list.
includes: Brush-script thank-you on striped stock
Single cards or a matched set
Ribbon wrap for a set
Names added when the set is for one event
madeFor: After a dinner, a shower, or a wedding weekend
Shop counters and market tables
Anyone who wants the pile of blank cards gone
note: Tell me if this is one card or a set, and whether each card needs a name.

title: Family Notes
summary: Mother’s Day, a note for dad, and the postage-stamp florals saved for the people who raised you.
story: Family notes are the cards with a specific person in mind. A gingham frame and a short sentence for dad. A floral stamp that just says mom. A Mother’s Day piece in periwinkle script on a striped ground. They are not a generic family category — each one is lettered for one relationship.
includes: Lettering written for one person
Floral, gingham, or striped artwork
A short line on the front, space to write inside
Holiday and just-because versions
madeFor: Mother’s Day and Father’s Day
Parents, grandparents, and the friend who is family
A note that does not need a holiday at all
note: Tell me who it is for and the sentence you want them to read first.

title: Holiday Cards
summary: Candles, ribbon, and quiet script for the December card you send in your own handwriting’s cousin.
story: Holiday pieces lean softer: taper candles with burgundy bows, a line of script around the margin, or a little tree and a short Christmas greeting. They can be one card for the mantel or a small batch with your family name worked into the lettering.
includes: A seasonal illustration
Script greeting, with your names if you want them
One card or a small mailed batch
Colors pulled from your table, not a catalog red
madeFor: Christmas and winter notes
Hostess cards for a holiday table
A mantel piece that is also a card
note: Share the greeting, any names, and whether you need one or a batch.

title: Illustrated Occasion Cards
summary: Fruit, objects, and one-off drawings — the cards that start as a picture and end as a sentence.
story: Some cards are more drawing than stationery. A gingham still life. A single object that means something to two people. A joke that only works if it is illustrated. These are the pieces that also show up sleeved at Arizona markets, and they can be made as a one-off with your own line on it.
includes: An original illustrated front
Lettering that fits the drawing
A single custom card, or a small run of a design you love
Market-style sleeve on request
madeFor: Inside jokes
A housewarming or a new apartment
Anyone who wants a drawing, not a verse
note: Describe the object, the joke, or the moment. A rough photo is welcome.

title: Welcome Signs
summary: The first thing guests read. A short phrase, a border with some nerve, and lettering that feels like the room.
story: Welcome signs do one job: tell people they are in the right place. The lettering is large, the phrase is short, and the border does as much work as the words — tile, stripe, floral, or a flat color from the palette of the day. Weddings, showers, dinners, and shop doors all start here.
includes: A hand-lettered welcome phrase
Names, a date, or a place name if you want them
A border drawn to match the rest of the day
Sizing talked through before anything is made
madeFor: Wedding and shower entrances
Dinner parties and backyard gatherings
A studio, shop, or front door
note: Send the exact words, where it will stand, and the date of the event.

title: Date & Detail Signs
summary: Names and a date, lettered so the day looks like a poster instead of a template.
story: A date sign is the piece people photograph. The numerals get room to breathe, the names sit in script, and the ground color belongs to the event — a wash of blush, a deep green, a paper cream. It can be the only sign of the day, or the one that sets the type style for everything else.
includes: Names and the date, hand-lettered
A ground and a small illustration if you want one
Wording for a wedding, a party, or a milestone
A size chosen for where it will be seen
madeFor: Weddings and engagement parties
Birthdays with a real date on them
Any day you want written down beautifully
note: Send the names exactly as you want them spelled, and the date.

title: Menus, Place Cards & Seating
summary: The paper on the table: a menu, a place card, a table number, all in the same hand.
story: Day-of paper is where event signage gets specific. A menu with the courses in script and the dishes in a steady serif. Place cards with a single name large enough to read when you sit down. Table numbers that match the welcome sign instead of fighting it. Ordered together, they look like one set.
includes: Menus, place cards, table numbers, or a mix
One lettering style across the set
Your wording, spelled the way you wrote it
Counts confirmed before the set is made
madeFor: Seated dinners and receptions
Showers and rehearsal dinners
A long table that needs to feel finished
note: Send the guest list or the menu as text, plus how many of each piece.

title: Full Event Suites
summary: Welcome, date, menu, and place cards drawn as one family instead of four separate orders.
story: A suite is the whole lettering for one event, planned together. The welcome sign, the date, the menu, and the place cards share a hand, a palette, and a border. You are not collecting mismatched prints. You are walking into a day that was lettered on purpose. This is the piece to ask for when the signage has to feel like the cards on the table.
includes: A shared palette and lettering style
Welcome sign and date sign
Day-of paper: menu, places, table numbers as needed
One round of wording changes before it is final
madeFor: Weddings that want every paper piece to match
Showers and milestone parties
Hosts who do not want to art-direct five vendors
note: Start with the date, the venue, and a list of which signs you actually need. We can leave pieces out.
